brief: OpenAI cut the valuation target for its in-progress funding round to $1.25 trillion from an initial $1.4 trillion ask, after Morgan Stanley and Dragoneer found weak demand ('zero clamouring' versus past 'frenzy') pitching private wealth clients. The round, up to $30 billion, is now expected to be led by Coatue and UAE funds, with commitments due October 30. This follows Anthropic investors discussing a ~$1.5 trillion valuation for its November IPO, down from $2 trillion previously penciled in. Together the two labs have cut about $650 billion off hoped valuations in a week, against a backdrop of an AI-driven market selloff: Thursday saw the S&P fall 1.2% and Nasdaq tumble 2.9%, hedge funds' worst day since 2011 by one Goldman measure, Goldman's AI basket down 23% from June highs, and credit spreads approaching March 2026 peaks that Goldman now expects to overshoot. Goldman's Rich Privorotsky frames the move as a repricing of the cost of capital rather than a demand problem. JPMorgan reports very low positioning but stays 'Tactically Bullish.' Both companies' pending IPOs, plus next week's MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN earnings, are now seen as the proof points the market needs.
